previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and microscopic colitis, was admitted for fatigue, crampy abdominal pain, and worsening diarrhea that progressed to 5–6 episodes per day. She had increased her prednisone dose without improvement. Labs showed hyponatremia (sodium 129) and hyperkalemia (potassium 5.1), consistent with an adrenal insufficiency flare. She was treated with triple-dose prednisone (15 mg), then transitioned to 10 mg daily per endocrine recommendation. A gluten-free diet was initiated due to concern for celiac disease, and TTG antibodies were ordered. Her symptoms resolved during the hospital stay. She remained stable on metoprolol for hypertension and levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. The patient was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue prednisone 10 mg daily, follow a gluten-free diet, and attend outpatient follow-up with endocrinology and her primary care provider.
